name: TPG Uncensored

date.source: The results thread's own subtitle, “TPG Uncensored Results, 10/9/05”.

notes: Eight matches and eight segments, three of the matches first-round ties in an International Championship tournament, and four of the eight written out in full while the rest run as one-line results. Called on the night by “Mean” Gene Okerland and Jesse “The Body” Ventura; the ring announcer is never named. The results thread's own replies carry a losing competitor disputing the outcome of the six-way — “i don't see how shaw won when my post was longer and more detailed than his” — and the booker answering that complaints should come to him privately.

matches.note: The card bills the losing side as Chill Factor.
Won with a Pedigree and a Springboard Swanton.

The card gives the result as a single line and no stipulation; six men are named in one bout. Zack Bowman's own roleplay a week later calls it “your one fall battle royal” and blames Rupert Shaw for ending his undefeated start (/promotions/pwe-inc/archive/shaw-bowman-heat-alden-vs-gid-bob-dude-explosion-2005-10-10.html).
Ended the undefeated streak David D and Tom Danials had gone on camera to talk about earlier the same night.
The card lists the match without a result; the fed's own commentary calls it “a big, easy win for Trish Stratus and So Cal Val”.
Won with a chokeslam and two Hopping Tombstones, the second for the fall.
Won with help from the Inquisitor, who had wrestled earlier the same night.

appearances.note: Three backstage interviews across the night.
On camera with David D talking about their undefeated streak.
Came to the ring to announce that the International Title match at Golden Opportunity would be a ladder match.
The card's own billing for the losing side of the opening six-man; its three members carry their own match rows.
Called the night alongside Jesse Ventura; the fed spells the name Okerland.

name: TPG: End of an Era III — Hour 3

date.source: The thread's own posting date and its own on-screen framing at Madison Square Garden.

notes: The third hour of the fed's own December supercard, and the only hour captured: a Diva Championship change, a number one contender's match, the return of the promotion's founder, and a World Championship crowned. Called by Paul Heyman and Roddy Piper. The page closes on the booker apologising for the results being ten minutes late because he had deleted the battle royal and had to rewrite it. Nine matches were booked for the night on the fed's own roleplay forum; the six that fell in the first two hours are carried here as billings and nothing more. One of those six, the battle royal, has its winner attested twice in this page's own replies — the winning member writes “I wasn't really expecting to win with only two roleplays” and thanks the field for “such a tough debut match”, and a beaten entrant congratulates him by name — but the thread names him only by his board handle, so no character is minted and no match row is written. The same replies record two roster departures: the handler of Randy Orton giving the character up, and Brock Mathews leaving the promotion with this show as his last.

matches.note: Pinfall in 3:57, off a flapjack slam. The document numbers this Match#8 and numbers the next match Match#8 as well; the numbering is the writer's own.

matches.stipulation: International Championship number one contender's match
matches.note: Pinfall in 9:59, off the Bombs Away, after David D answered a slow count with a low blow.
Pinfall in 9:56, off a frog splash from the top rope thrown as a tribute under the Guerrero banner.

appearances.note: Took the microphone from the fed's own interviewer to hand it to Kris Adams, and was in the ring for the celebration.
Interfered in the World Championship match and was dropped on his head for it.
Returned as the fed's own founder and left with a Hell on Earth match booked for January.
Came out with the World Championship belt to answer the founder, and staked the International Championship on the match he made.
Opened a backstage interview with Kris Adams and had the microphone taken out of her hand by Rachel Taylor before she finished her first sentence.

name: Farmageddon

evidence.source: the board's own ARCHIVES category as it rendered on 15 December 2005 (/promotions/pwe-inc/archive/forum-pwe-inc-archives-59.html)
evidence.note: The board's own ARCHIVES category carries a Farmageddon forum of 20 topics and 274 replies, described “Come see what we have all been waiting for. The clash of The Proving Grounds and Foundation of Brutality. It's all inside.”, last posted 28 September 2005 in a topic titled FARMAGEDDON MATCH WRITING.

notes: The Proving Grounds against the Foundation of Brutality, the two farm leagues that shared the board. Its own forum was archived by December 2005; no card, no result and no date beyond the archive's own last-post line survives. The fed was still running it two years later.

notes: Called the fed's own annual pay-per-view by the board that hosted it. It was still taking posts on the last day the record covers.
